name: Do side-house additions need a permit in Glendale or Pasadena?

mainEntity.name: Do side-house additions need a permit in Glendale or Pasadena?
mainEntity.text: Do side-house additions need a permit in Glendale or Pasadena?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, most side-house additions need permits in Glendale, Pasadena, and neighboring Los Angeles-area cities. Because a side addition usually changes the building footprint and often affects structural framing, foundations, electrical, plumbing, or mechanical systems, it is rarely a permit-exempt project. The city may require a plan check before issuing the permit, along with site plans, structural details, and trade documents. Depending on the property, additional reviews can come up for drainage, grading, fire access, or historic-district considerations. Homeowners sometimes assume a small side expansion is simple enough to skip permits, but unpermitted additions can create problems during resale, appraisal, insurance claims, or future remodels. If the property is in unincorporated county territory rather than a city boundary, the permit process can differ. The safest approach is to verify jurisdiction first, then confirm exactly which permits and approvals the project needs before construction begins.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes. A side-house addition that adds square footage, changes the footprint, or affects structural systems typically needs a building permit and plan review in Glendale or Pasadena. Trade permits may also be required for electrical, plumbing, HVAC, and gas work.
